name: Sacituzumab govitecan (single agent)
cyclesNote: Given on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle, continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Later-line option after platinum and a checkpoint inhibitor (typically after enfortumab vedotin).

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Sacituzumab govitecan is a Trop-2-directed antibody-drug conjugate delivering an SN-38 (topoisomerase I inhibitor) payload. Trop-2 is broadly expressed in urothelial carcinoma and no companion biomarker test is required to treat.

premedications.name: Antiemetic and infusion-reaction prophylaxis
premedications.notes: premedicate with antipyretics, H1/H2 blockers, and corticosteroids to reduce infusion reactions; give antiemetic prophylaxis (moderate-to-high emetic risk).

supportiveCare: NEUTROPENIA: monitor CBC before each dose; consider granulocyte colony-stimulating factor support for severe or febrile neutropenia.
DIARRHEA: treat promptly with loperamide; evaluate for infectious causes and hold for severe diarrhea.
Reduced UGT1A1 activity increases toxicity risk - monitor closely and reduce dose for severe reactions.
Monitor for infusion reactions during and after administration.
monitoring: assessment for diarrhea and dehydration each visit

doseModificationRules.text: Hold until recovery and reduce dose per labeling for grade 4 neutropenia or febrile neutropenia; add growth-factor support. Physician decides.
Hold for grade 3-4 diarrhea, treat with anti-diarrheals and fluids, and reduce dose on recovery per labeling; obtain clinical review.

drugs.name: Sacituzumab govitecan
drugs.notes: Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle. Neutropenia and diarrhea are the principal dose-limiting toxicities. Dose per standard urothelial later-line practice (Standard Guidelines / DeVita / Harrison, general reference).

provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy, Trop-2 ADC later-line
